The first PR should implement [step 1 in PLAN.md](/home/peterc/jev-orchestrator/PLAN.md:145):

- Introduce provider-neutral configuration, types, and errors, reusing the existing contract and bounded transports.
- Add `ROUTER_PROVIDER`, preserve `JEV_PROVIDER` and credential aliases, and reject conflicting selectors.
- Resolve provider/model selection **once per run** and retain it through recovery. Evaluation currently resolves configuration on every call.
- Update CLI labels, attribution, documentation, and regression tests while preserving trace compatibility.

Keep direct TypeSafe/Jev as the default and preserve all policy thresholds, approvals, validation requirements, and budgets.

After that, the planned sequence is **Clef/Clef-flash → OpenAI Decisions through OpenRouter → shared regressions → opt-in live verification → labeled model comparison → release packaging**.

No live credentials are needed to start the first PR. Before release, we’ll need verified Cloudflare account access and OpenRouter model access, plus sanitized live-check and comparison evidence. Provider response contracts should be rechecked during adapter implementation.

No source files changed during this assessment.

+# Decision snapshot comparison
+
+This v0.3 study evaluates the four decision models against the same 14 synthetic
+coding-task snapshots. It invokes the existing evaluator and policy, and checks
+worker candidates for selection/call budgets. It executes no repository tool,
+validation command, or coding worker. Recommendations remain unexecuted.
+
+`fixtures.mjs` fixes labels before live evaluation. Cases cover unread issues
+and instructions, both worker selections, missing acceptance criteria, stuck
+work, failed/stale/pending validation, exhausted workers, redundant tests,
+baseline-only tests, accepted completion, and explicit evaluation recovery.
+Failed validation permits either reading the known failing file or delegating
+a bounded repair. Other cases have a single reference action. Predicate labels
+are omitted where their interpretation is ambiguous. Labels and rationales are
+never sent to a model. These hand-authored labels are a small project-specific
+reference set, not universal ground truth for coding workflows.
+
+The fixed routes are direct TypeSafe `jev-latest`, Cloudflare `clef` and
+`clef-flash`, and OpenRouter `openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions`. Keep the production
+TypeSafe default and all approval, worker, iteration, validation, and confidence
+controls unchanged. Provider prerequisites and data handling are documented in
+[README](../../README.md#evaluation-providers). Only synthetic snapshot evidence
+is sent to those services. The comparison needs the existing TypeSafe,
+Cloudflare, and OpenRouter credentials, plus the Cloudflare account ID.
+
+```bash
+pnpm build
+pnpm compare:decisions --plan
+
+# The parent exists; the output directory must be new and outside the checkout.
+# Use Varlock to load local credentials, including encrypted values.
+pnpm env:run node scripts/decisions/run.mjs --live /external/new-output 3
+```
+
+The live opt-in is mandatory. Repetitions are bounded to 1–3, defaulting to 3.
+The default schedules 168 evaluations, at most 336 HTTP attempts, sequentially.
+Route order rotates by snapshot and repetition. Each evaluator retains the
+production 10-second deadline, one transient retry, and 64 KiB response limit;
+the study also stops after 15 minutes. Configuration is bound once per route.
+Input and question hashes verify identical bounded evidence on every HTTP
+attempt. A mismatch stops the study. Existing output directories are refused.
+
+SIGINT/SIGTERM cancels the current evaluation and stops scheduling. Every
+completed/failed/interrupted observation is retained, along with planned and
+unstarted counts. There is no automatic replacement of failures or executable
+resume. A complete comparison includes all scheduled observations, even failures.
+Changing labels, prompts, or protocol requires a new study version and cohort.
+
+The output contains a manifest, bounded inputs with separate labels, copied
+harness sources, allowlisted observations, and aggregate JSON. Source HEAD,
+working-tree status, runtime/harness hashes, served models, and input identity
+are recorded. Credentials, headers, account IDs/URLs, raw provider bodies,
+error messages, and refusal text are excluded. Usage keeps only explicitly
+returned nonnegative integer token counts, with coverage counts. Missing usage
+stays unknown; no cost estimate or provider price assumption is made.
+
+Reporting separates raw routing correctness, policy correctness, worker-guard
+correctness, forbidden recommendations/selections, policy/candidate overrides,
+abstentions, and acceptance-review candidates. A forbidden action is one that
+violates the fixture's preparation, worker, validation, or completion boundary;
+it does not mean an unsafe action was executed. Abstention/manual-review counts
+are potential operator interventions; no operator alternatives are exercised.
+Failures remain in the attempted denominator. Refusals are counted only when
+an explicit refusal shape was observed; other invalid responses are not guessed
+to be refusals. Per-snapshot results retain all repetitions.
+
+Multiclass action Brier is the sum of squared errors over the known actions,
+without renormalization; the set-valued repair case is excluded. Predicate
+Brier uses only labeled predicates. Five-bin reliability tables compare chosen
+action probability and, separately, provider confidence with empirical routing
+correctness. Confidence semantics differ across APIs, so its alignment is a
+diagnostic, not proof that confidence is a calibrated probability. Missing
+confidence is excluded with an explicit sample count. Timing uses the local
+monotonic clock and includes transport, bounded response instrumentation,
+retries, and backoff. All-attempt and normalized-only latency distributions have

+## 0.3.0 — multiple decision models
+
+Release candidate prepared on 2026-10-16. Tagging and publication are pending.
+The package remains `jev-orchestrator`, the executable remains `jev-agent`,
+and Node.js 22+ is required.
+
+### Added
+
+- Cloudflare Clef and Clef-flash through a bounded Workers AI REST adapter.
+- OpenAI Decisions through the existing OpenRouter Decisions transport.
+- Provider-neutral configuration, evaluation, and errors, retaining Jev-named
+  exports and environment aliases for compatibility.
+- Shared transport, policy, and orchestration regressions across all six
+  provider/model routes, plus explicit opt-in synthetic verification.
+- Pinned Varlock development tooling with sensitive credential schemas and
+  redacted checks. Installed consumers do not need Varlock at runtime.
+- A labeled decision comparison with 168 live evaluations across 14 workflow
+  states, reporting routing, policy overrides, failures, latency, returned usage,
+  and separate probability/confidence diagnostics.
+
+### Configuration and migration
+
+Set `ROUTER_PROVIDER` explicitly to choose a transport. With neither selector
+set, direct TypeSafe/Jev remains the default. Only the selected provider's
+credentials are required; there is no automatic failover.
+
+| Decision model | `ROUTER_PROVIDER` | `ROUTER_MODEL` | Required environment |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Jev / TypeSafe (default) | `typesafe` | `jev-latest` (default), or `jev-1.13.0` | `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or `TYPESAFE_AI_API_KEY` |
+| Jev / OpenRouter | `openrouter` | `typesafe/jev-1.13` (default) | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTE_API_KEY` |
+| Jev / Vercel | `vercel` | `typesafe-ai/jev` (default) | `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` |
+| Clef / Clef-flash | `cloudflare` | `clef` (default) or `clef-flash` | `CLOUDFLARE_AUTH_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` |
+| OpenAI Decisions | `openrouter` | `openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions` | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTE_API_KEY` |
+
+Existing `JEV_PROVIDER` configurations still work. If both selectors are set,
+they must agree; conflicting, empty, or unknown selectors fail before a request.
+For the earlier Gateway behavior, explicitly select `vercel`. Clear an old
+`ROUTER_MODEL` override when changing providers or replace it with a model in
+the new provider's namespace. `OPENROUTE_MODEL` remains an OpenRouter-only
+fallback when `ROUTER_MODEL` is blank. Nonblank canonical keys take precedence
+over credential aliases. Direct OpenAI transport and credentials are outside
+this release.
+
+Results and traces include `provider`, `requestedModel`, and an optional
+`servedModel`, while preserving existing schema versions and the `model` field.
+The Gateway's unverified served version stays absent. Existing `mock/jev` and
+`jev_finish` labels remain compatible.
+
+### Prerequisites and data handling
+
+The selected account needs model access and billing capacity. Cloudflare
+requires a 32-character hexadecimal account ID and an account-scoped Workers AI
+token with Read and Edit permissions. OpenAI Decisions uses an OpenRouter key;
+it does not require a direct OpenAI key. Vercel access was not established for
+the tested account; authorization failure is retained as an access limitation.
+

+## v0.6 draft: saved runs and safe resume
+
+Drafted on 2026-10-17 at the operator's request to plan v0.6. Saved runs and
+safe resume are the proposed focus, building on v0.4's workflow behavior and
+v0.5's presentation work. This is a design proposal; implementation has not
+started and the published CLI has no resume command.
+
+The intended outcome is to stop an opted-in orchestration run, close the
+terminal, and later continue the same task without reconstructing its context
+or losing track of consumed limits. A local history view should explain what
+happened, what remains, and whether continuation is possible. An existing
+task's partial edits stay in its working tree.
+
+### User workflow and first-release boundary
+
+Provisional command shape, to be finalized with CLI compatibility tests:
+
+```text
+dev-agent . "Fix the bug and add regression tests" --orchestrate --save-run
+dev-agent --list-runs
+dev-agent --show-run <run-id>
+dev-agent --resume <run-id>
+```
+
+Saving is opt-in for orchestration. Listing and showing runs are read-only
+local operations with bounded output. `--resume` explicitly reopens a saved
+orchestration run; every resolved action still requires approval. Keep these
+options distinct from existing repository/task positional arguments, and keep
+decision-only behavior unchanged. Run IDs resolve only inside the application's
+run store; they are not arbitrary file paths or shell arguments.
+
+The first release supports continuation on the same machine and canonical
+repository/worktree after a typed stop, an evaluation-failure stop, or a signal
+interruption whose process cleanup completed. Finished runs and runs at the
+iteration limit remain inspectable. Resume cannot grant extra iterations or
+worker calls. A new task with a new budget is a separate explicit run.
+
+An unclean termination with an unresolved execution is inspectable but cannot
+resume execution in this first slice. Never replay an uncertain action, assume
+an orphaned worker has exited, or roll back partial edits. Cross-machine
+transfer, background workers, worker-native conversation restoration, and
+automatic retry after a crash are later scope.
+
+### Saved-run and continuation contract
+
+- Store a bounded, versioned checkpoint separately from JSONL traces. Current
+  traces truncate values and arrays and cannot reconstruct complete state;
+  neither old nor new traces become executable resume inputs. Freeze the
+  checkpoint's schema, size limits, status transitions, and compatibility rules
+  before integrating execution. Unsupported versions must fail explicitly.
+- Preserve the original task, bounded approved context and its provenance,
+  repository identity, instruction/validation metadata, frozen provider/model,
+  worker selection and network permission, consumed budgets, and failure
+  history. Keep transport objects, credentials, raw environment values,
+  AbortSignal, and executable approval objects out of the format. Record only
+  non-secret configuration identity; reload credentials from the operator's
+  environment and reject provider/account or permission changes during resume.
+- Use an operator-owned application state directory outside worker-writable
+  repositories, with restricted access, bounded reads, and atomic checkpoint
+  replacement. Define integrity and sequence checks against an authoritative
+  local attempt ledger. Validate persisted content as untrusted input; a
+  checksum by itself is not authorization. Reject malformed, truncated,
+  altered, or stale checkpoints instead of repairing counters or flags.
+- Record iteration consumption before evaluation and reserve worker allowance
+  durably before dispatch. Record outcomes without charging the same attempt
+  twice. An uncertain reserved attempt stays charged and is reported as
+  uncertain, without inventing a successful execution or an approval. If a
+  required durable write fails, start no further evaluation or execution;
+  drain any active cleanup and explain the last trustworthy checkpoint.
+- Acquire exclusive ownership of the saved run and prevent another app-managed
+  run from using the same worktree concurrently. An unresolved active owner or
+  stale lock blocks execution; never kill a process based only on a saved PID.
+  The design must account for process cleanup before a run becomes resumable.
+- Refresh repository state before continuation. A different worktree, changed
+  HEAD, unavailable repository, or unbounded/ambiguous identity check blocks
+  resume. Show any working-tree drift, retain historical evidence as historical,
+  and use the existing clarification/preparation gates when task context needs
+  review. Changed instruction files require new bounded reads and approval.
+  Do not restore Git state, replace files, or revert operator edits.
+- Start a fresh validation generation on resume; prior passing checks remain
+  history and cannot authorize completion. Rebuild candidates from current
+  state and require new approvals, including acceptance review for `FINISH`.
+  Resume of an evaluation failure retains its explicit recovery requirement.
+  A saved proposal, old approval, or worker test claim grants no authority.
+- Retain the eight-iteration and two-calls-per-adapter ceilings across every
+  process segment. Selection and permission flags remain immutable; fresh
+  validation also consumes the remaining budget. Insufficient budget must
+  produce the existing bounded stop rather than silently extend the run.
+  Link segment traces and summaries by run identity while keeping metrics
+  outside authorization state. Measure active time with each process's local
+  monotonic clock; time between sessions is not active work or prompt wait.
+
+### Implementation order
+
+1. [ ] Define the checkpoint schema, attempt ledger, storage bounds, and
+   lifecycle. Document exactly which fields are restored, revalidated, or
+   historical, and how integrity, write ordering, locks, and compatibility are
+   enforced. Add offline fixtures for clean stops, exhausted limits, incomplete
+   writes, altered counters/permissions, stale checkpoints, and unresolved
+   executions. No execution path may accept a saved record until this contract
+   is validated.
+2. [ ] Add opt-in persistence to the existing orchestration lifecycle. Persist
+   budget reservations before dispatch and completed transitions afterward;
+   preserve existing signal cleanup and trace behavior. Test failures before
+   and after each durable boundary so restarting cannot duplicate execution,
+   reset budgets, or lose an in-flight attempt from the record.
+3. [ ] Add local run listing and inspection with the plain and styled CLI
+   presentation. Show task/repository identity, last status, remaining budgets,
+   pending validation, failure/interruption, and a specific resume blocker.
+   These commands must not call a provider, invoke a worker, or change the
+   selected repository. Keep context bounded and credentials redacted.
+4. [ ] Add explicit resume for eligible saved runs. Resolve the same repository
+   and immutable configuration, obtain exclusive ownership, refresh evidence,
+   invalidate validation, and enter the loop at the next unconsumed iteration.
+   Retain approved clarification provenance and failure history; require the
+   existing action, recovery, and completion decisions. Incompatible or
+   incomplete records remain inspectable without being executable.
+5. [ ] Verify and prepare v0.6.0. Exercise stop/restart/resume through mocked
+   provider/process boundaries for both workers and all supported routes, plus
+   an operator-authorized live stop/resume walkthrough for each worker. Cover
+   cancellation, EOF, changed worktrees/instructions, missing credentials,
+   storage failures, concurrent resumes, and exhausted budgets. Run focused
+   tests, typecheck, the full suite, build, schema validation, and installed
+   package checks; document migration, local storage, and known limits. Record
+   release source and archive evidence, give advance npm authentication notice,
+   and verify publication through a separate registry installation.
+
+### Release gate
+
+- [ ] A cleanly stopped saved run resumes in a new CLI process, preserves task
+  context and remaining limits, and finishes only after fresh validation and
+  explicit acceptance approval. Both worker adapters are covered.
+- [ ] Old approvals, changed permissions, wrong repository identity, tampered
+  or incompatible state, unresolved attempts, and concurrent owners cannot
+  cause execution. Exhausted budgets cannot be reset through resume.
+- [ ] Failure-injection tests establish durable write ordering and conservative
+  attempt accounting. Trace compatibility, credential exclusion, cleanup, and
+  preservation of operator edits pass their regressions.
+- [ ] History and both presentation modes clearly distinguish resumable,
+  blocked, finished, and budget-exhausted runs. The exact installed package and
+  recorded live walkthroughs pass before release.
+

+# v0.4 routing explanations
+
+The second v0.4 slice adds plain, grouped explanations to orchestration review,
+evaluation recovery, and terminal results. It uses the
+[offline workflow baseline](v0.4-baseline.md) to exercise reporting alongside
+the existing enforcement layers. No terminal library is added in this slice.
+
+## Reading an action review
+
+Each approval review separates five things:
+
+1. **Model recommendation:** requested action, exact choice/confidence values,
+   task-completion probability, provider/model attribution, and distribution.
+   Missing confidence is reported as unavailable; no value is inferred.
+2. **Policy decision:** the selected action, override status, and policy reason.
+3. **Candidate review:** the action that could actually be resolved, its tool
+   and parseable parameters, and any candidate blocker. A manual alternative
+   is identified separately from the original policy selection.
+4. **Current evidence and limits:** issue/clarification provenance, unread
+   instructions, current-generation check outcomes, bounded failure evidence,
+   worker limits/selection, remaining iterations, and interaction counters.
+5. **Operator choices:** the loop's allowed action names and how to review,
+   approve, reject, stop, provide context, or confirm task acceptance.
+
+The allowed names are choices to resolve and review. Selecting a name can
+still produce a blocked candidate; it never approves execution. The displayed
+parameters retain their existing JSON representation, with secrets redacted
+and terminal control bytes escaped. Explanatory strings and check lists are
+bounded and rendered as plain lines.
+
+Example excerpt: a low-confidence worker recommendation after preparation.
+The complete review also prints attribution, distribution, and parameters.
+
+```text
+Iteration 3 of 8 (6 remaining, including this iteration)
+Model recommendation
+Evaluator requested: CALL_CODEX
+Choice probability: 1; reported confidence: 0.1.
+Task-completion probability: 0.02.
+
+Policy decision
+Policy selected: ASK_USER (override)
+Reason: The next-action distribution is too ambiguous for autonomous execution.
+
+Candidate review
+Resolving policy selection: ASK_USER.
+Safe candidate: ASK_USER
+
+Current evidence and limits
+Independent checks (generation 0): test: pending, lint: pending.
+Worker calls used: Codex 0/2; Claude 0/2.
+Interaction totals: 2 action approvals; 0 manual alternatives; 0 explicit evaluation recoveries.
+```
+
+If the operator selects `CALL_CODEX`, its next review says:
+
+```text
+Manual alternative requested: CALL_CODEX; original policy selection: ASK_USER.
+Safe candidate: CALL_CODEX
+```
+
+It still shows the original recommendation and confidence. Execution requires
+approval of that resolved candidate. If the candidate cannot be offered, the
+review instead names the unavailable action and prints the candidate reason.
+
+## Baseline cases and operator choices
+
+| Situation | Explanation | Operator choice |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Linked issue or instructions not read | Shows the requested worker, preparation policy override, exact resolved read, and remaining unread instruction names. | Review and approve the read, choose another listed action for review, or stop. |
+| Issue unavailable / blank clarification | States that operator task context is still required. Accepted replacement context is attributed to clarification. | Approve `ASK_USER` and supply acceptance criteria, or stop. |
+| Missing or low routing confidence | Shows the reported confidence exactly, or `not reported`, alongside the policy override. | Supply context or select a listed alternative and separately approve its resolved candidate. |
+| Independent validation failed | Names failed/pending checks in the current generation and displays bounded, redacted failure diagnostics. | Diagnose through a listed read/worker/context action and review the resulting candidate. An unchanged failed candidate may remain unavailable. |
+| Worker returned failure, timeout, or partial work | Reports the unsuccessful attempt, retained call usage, and fresh validation requirements. | Review saved edits and obtain separately approved independent validation. |
+| Prior checks are stale | Names the new generation and explicitly says older results cannot cover its pending checks. | Review the pending independent check candidate. |
+| Required check absent / context omitted requirements | Shows missing runnable coverage or the omitted-requirements blocker. Passing detected checks does not clear it. | Obtain enough task/repository context to resolve the missing requirement, or stop. |
+| Package manager unknown / inspection refresh failed | Names the specific validation or inspection blocker. | Provide approved context/recover inspection or stop. |
+| Worker call limit reached | Separates the confident recommendation, policy selection, and unavailable candidate; names the exhausted limit and fixed worker selection. | Choose an offered inspection/context action or stop; no additional worker call is granted. |
+| All checks passed, model repeats tests | Explains the policy-owned acceptance review and identifies a manual `FINISH` selection separately. | Select `FINISH`, review it, and approve only if the original task acceptance criteria are met. |
+| Evaluation failed | No candidate/approval is attributed to the failed evaluation. Shows retained checks/call usage and iterations available for explicit recovery. | Enter `continue` for a fresh evaluation or `stop`; continuation consumes another iteration and grants no action approval. |
+| Budget ended after a validated repair | States that independent checks passed but completion approval did not fit within the iteration budget. | Review the saved patch/checks/trace. A separate invocation is a new run with its own approvals. |
+| Typed stop or interruption | States that the run ended without claiming completion and preserves edits/evidence. Signal exits identify interruption. | Review saved work and diagnostics before explicitly starting another run. |
+
+Action approvals, manual alternatives, and explicit evaluation recoveries have
+separate counters during review and in the final summary. Choosing an
+alternative is not counted as approving it. Evaluation failure/recovery is
+separate from action approval. Passing validation and approved task acceptance
+remain separate outcomes.
+
+## Reporting and compatibility boundary
+
+The loop supplies a copied, display-only `ApprovalContext.review` snapshot
+with review provenance, the actual iteration limit, and existing metric counts.
+It is never read by policy, candidate selection, final approval enforcement,
+or execution. It cannot grant permissions or replenish any budget.

+# v0.4 repair routing candidate
+
+This candidate fixes one deterministic detour in the testing-priority rule.
+It uses a labeled variant of the frozen `short-label-repair` task from the
+[offline baseline](v0.4-baseline.md). Task source, acceptance criteria, worker
+patches, checks, and the original recommendation sequences remain unchanged.
+The reserved verification task is not used here.
+
+## Reproduction and change
+
+After a worker's first patch, independent testing finds the boundary bug. The
+next synthetic assessment confidently recommends returning to that worker and
+also reports `needsTesting: 0.99`. Both values are retained exactly.
+
+Previously, the high testing score entered the validation-priority rule. That
+rule saw a failed check and selected `ASK_USER`, even though the recommendation
+already named a useful repair action and the independent failure supplied the
+needed diagnostic evidence. An operator had to select the worker manually or
+provide unnecessary clarification to advance that recommendation.
+
+Policy now offers the recommended worker candidate for separate approval when:
+
+- The action probability and reported confidence clear the existing thresholds.
+- Linked-task preparation is complete, repository inspection is available, and
+  missing-information/stuck assessments do not require operator input.
+- The recommendation names the same worker as the preceding implementation
+  attempt, that worker is allowed for the run, and a call remains available.
+- Required validation is failed, and a failed independent check in the current
+  generation was recorded after that worker attempt and before this evaluation.
+
+Worker text, earlier-generation results, and a failure recorded before the
+worker cannot establish this exception. With no fresh independent check, the
